claims.text: A high-strength ceramic matrix containing an embedded layered solid lubricant can provide stable self-lubricating performance over a wide temperature range.
Integrating WS2 nanosheets into a TiN matrix can balance high mechanical strength with effective lubrication.
TiN is a high-strength ceramic matrix material.
Unmodified TiN lacks significant lubrication properties.
WS2 nanosheets act as a solid-lubricant phase in a TiN matrix.
WS2 nanosheets can form a lubricious transfer film at sliding interfaces.
The TiN matrix maintains the composite's mechanical strength and structural integrity.
The layered structure of WS2 permits easy interlayer shear under frictional stress.
Easy interlayer shear in WS2 reduces friction over a range of temperatures.
The TiN matrix resists deformation and wear.
Resistance to deformation and wear by TiN keeps the WS2 lubricant well dispersed.
At high temperatures, thermally stable TiN prevents excessive degradation of WS2.
WS2 provides high-temperature lubrication through temperature-dependent transfer-film formation.
A TiN-WS2 composite will have a lower friction coefficient than pure TiN across a wide temperature range.
A TiN-WS2 composite will exhibit less wear than pure TiN across a wide temperature range.
A TiN-WS2 composite will retain high mechanical strength.
Pure TiN exhibits higher friction and wear than the proposed TiN-WS2 composite over a range of temperatures.
Self-lubricating effectiveness may decline above the decomposition or phase-transition temperatures of WS2.
Self-lubricating effectiveness may decline under loads outside the range required for WS2 transfer-film formation.
WS2 dispersion, interfacial bonding, and extreme-temperature degradation can affect the composite's tribological performance.
